clue.text: Pillagers back up to eat snack prepared by Saxon's chief

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it inside, so these letters swallow the others
in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the back of something is its rear

indicators.note: food that is prepared is worked into shape, so these letters are rearranged
the chief part of a word is its head, its first letter

explanation.surface: Raiders turn the larder upside down and devour a snack laid out by the Saxon leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is a synonym and 'up' reverses it to RAER; 'to eat' then wraps the reworked snack, and 'chief' adds the Saxon's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: People who plunder a place are pillagers, searching and stripping it of valuables.

clue.text: Change 11p over old cover?

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the figures read as words: eleven, then p for pence

explanation.surface: A shopper asks for change from eleven pence for an old wrapper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges ELEVEN, P and O. The 11 is not a cross-reference here, though the grid has an 11-across; it is simply the number spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper envelope covers and encloses a letter; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Alternative fuel overwhelms fellow with unknown discharge

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so these letters close around another
an alternative arrangement of the letters of fuel, so they are rearranged

parts.note: X is the classic unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: An eco-fuel floods a man with some mystery leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative' turns FUEL into EFLU; 'overwhelms' puts F inside it, giving EFFLU, then X follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An efflux is an outflow of liquid or gas, which is what a discharge is.

clue.text: Woman to wed right away

indicators.note: going away means this letter leaves the word

parts.note: to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: A woman wants to get married immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads like 'at once', but it tells you to take R out of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary is a female first name, so a woman can be clued by it.

clue.text: Heavens above! On another planet 2001 computer is law enforcer

indicators.note: in a down clue, being above means this piece comes first

parts.note: the heavens are the sky
Mars is a planet other than Earth
HAL 9000 is the computer in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey

explanation.surface: A sci-fi exclamation: a computer from the film 2001 turns lawman on a distant planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens above!' looks like an exclamation, but 'Heavens' gives SKY and 'above' places it on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky marshal is an armed security officer travelling on aircraft to keep order, a kind of police officer.

clue.text: Has tan spoiled in afternoon shadow?

indicators.note: one set of letters goes inside another

parts.note: PM is the abbreviation for the afternoon (post meridiem)

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sunbather asks whether an afternoon in the shade has ruined their tan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges HASTAN; 'in' puts the result between P and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantasm is a ghostly apparition, and a shadow can be a spectre or wraith, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Keep players on leg-side boundaries

parts.note: the players in a show are its cast

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: A cricket captain stations fielders along the leg-side boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is the half of the field behind a right-hander's legs, and the boundary is the edge of the field; here they just give L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the stronghold tower of a fortress, so it stands for the whole fortification.

clue.text: Teacher admits time in prison

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: British pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A teacher confesses to having served a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' looks like a confession but is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is British slang for jail, as in doing time in stir.

clue.text: Old queen's honest with diarist

parts.note: Queen Anne reigned in Britain 1702-14
to be honest is to be frank

explanation.surface: A historic queen is candid with the person keeping a diary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jewish teenager whose wartime journal in hiding in Amsterdam is world-famous.

clue.text: Core of world back to front

indicators.note: the letter at the back moves to the front of the word

parts.note: the world we live on is the Earth

explanation.surface: The centre of the globe has been flipped round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' usually means a reversal, but here only the last letter, H, moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its centre or essence, its core.

clue.text: Poet recounts fifth item found on beach

indicators.note: to recount is to tell out loud, so the letters are said rather than spelt

parts.note: an item found on a beach is a shell, and the fifth letter of the alphabet is E, giving SHELL then E

explanation.surface: A poet tells the tale of the fifth thing picked up on the sands.
explanation.walkthrough: SHELL followed by the letter E, said out loud, gives the poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley was a major English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Rolling Stone caught by Mr Big? Very!

indicators.note: being caught by something is being held inside it
rolling about shakes the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A rock band member is nabbed by a crime boss, who is asked if he's big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stone' looks like the band, but 'Rolling' rearranges STONE, and MR holds the result.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective monster means huge, so 'very big' fits.

clue.text: Reportedly, get lost pastry

indicators.note: something reported is told by word of mouth, so the word is as heard

parts.note: shoo is an order to go away

explanation.surface: Supposedly a pastry has told someone to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: Choux is the light French dough used for eclairs and profiteroles.

clue.text: They're involved in father's Star Trek battle — once timeless

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: a battle throws things into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
a single time, abbreviated T, is taken away

explanation.surface: Dad's sci-fi war is an old battle that once had no end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once timeless' removes just one T from STAR TREK; 'battle' rearranges the remaining SARTREK.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who partake take part in something, being involved in it.

clue.text: Titan unearthed in built-up Rome? The usual!

indicators.note: dug out of the words, so the letters are found inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a great find dug up in crowded Rome as par for the course.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the last letter of 'built-up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prometheus was one of the Titans of Greek myth, who stole fire for humanity.

clue.text: Climbing mountains with quiet descent on landing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: the Alps are a European mountain range
sh is a call for quiet
going down is a descent

explanation.surface: A mountaineer climbs and then makes a quiet descent to land.
explanation.definitionFit: A splashdown is the landing of a spacecraft in the sea.

clue.text: Choose over Charlie or Michael involving a branch of science

parts.note: to choose is to elect

indicators.note: something knocked over is upset, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Picking between Charlie or Michael involves a scientific branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like a placement word but is the anagram signal, as in knocked over; 'or' joins the fodder as letters rather than acting as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrochemistry is the science of chemical change caused by electricity, so this adjective relates to that field.

clue.text: During Great Revolt, we English can be using social media

indicators.note: one piece comes during, so inside, the other
to revolt is to turn over, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: GT is the abbreviation for great
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: During a great uprising, English people can be posting online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolt' reverses GT to TG, which holds WE, E and TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweeting is posting short messages on the platform formerly called Twitter, a social network.

clue.text: Animal around and about, adult male's lost

parts.note: C, from circa, means around (a date)
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: something lost has gone, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: an adult is mature
M is the abbreviation for male; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A beast circles round and about, and the grown man has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature is any living being, especially an animal.

clue.text: Director left at the end holding hard part of shoe

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside
this letter is shifted to the end of the name

parts.note: Spike Lee is an American film director
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A film director, having walked out at the finish, is clutching a firm piece of footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' gives L, and 'at the end' shifts that L of the director's surname to the end, leaving SPIKEEEL; 'holding' then takes in H.
explanation.definitionFit: A spike heel is a tall thin stiletto heel, part of a woman's shoe.

clue.text: Every so often big cheat began to drink

indicators.note: only some letters at regular intervals are taken, here every second one

explanation.surface: Now and then a big cheat took up drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced tea served cold is a popular refreshing beverage, also called ice tea.

clue.text: Encounters aliens on Earth following Martian leader

indicators.note: the earlier piece is followed by the later ones
in an across clue, the aliens being on the Earth puts them after it
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ETs are extraterrestrials

explanation.surface: Visitors from space land on our planet after their Martian chief.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across someone is to encounter them, the same as meeting.

clue.text: Up-to-date style worn by sailors

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors are wearing a fashionable look.
explanation.definitionFit: Something modern is current and in the latest fashion.

clue.text: Revolutionary recalls loathing for large cat

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine revolutionary

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: loathing is hate

explanation.surface: A rebel remembers his disgust for a big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is a large spotted wild cat, the fastest land animal.

clue.text: In court, large expense

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: Going to law is a big outlay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cost is a price paid, an expense.

clue.text: Starts to smoke, eventually saw someone tranquillised

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: to see someone romantically is to date them

explanation.surface: A person takes up smoking, then finally starts dating and feels calmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sedated has been given a calming drug, tranquillised.

clue.text: Rising troubles with this kind of bread

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: ados are fusses or troubles

explanation.surface: Baking woes: a loaf that won't rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda bread is raised with bicarbonate of soda rather than yeast.

clue.text: Doubles taken from physicist's mug

indicators.note: taken from means removed from

parts.note: Albert Einstein was the physicist
the group E, I, N appears twice in the name, so one copy is a double

explanation.surface: Twin items have been stolen from a scientist's mug.
explanation.walkthrough: EIN occurs twice in EINSTEIN; removing the first copy leaves the drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stein is a large beer mug, often earthenware.

clue.text: To ensure sufficient funds remain below interest

parts.note: below means under
a draw is something that attracts interest

explanation.surface: Advice on keeping a bank balance healthy below the interest rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To underdraw an account is to take out less than is available, so money is left in it.
